items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: Your sugar rose about 26.0 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Walking after dinner can help with your sugar, which rose 26.0 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Try to walk for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, when the biggest gain of 18.3 mg/dL was seen.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: You only had dinner at 8 pm or later 16.7% of the time, which is good since sugar rose 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. Keep having dinner before 8 pm to avoid a rise in sugar.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged an overnight fast of 12.9 hours, with 50.0% of nights reaching 13 hours. Having an overnight fast was part of the coaching that changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared to coaching alone.
